experience.title: Software Engineer Intern
experience.summary: Sole engineer working directly with the CEO, rebuilding a healthcare and community-coordination platform for a Dallas–Fort Worth pilot where partner organizations coordinate care across referrals, cases, tasks, and consent-governed data sharing. Built four portals (staff, partner, patient, helper) on a single Next.js 16 / React 19 / TypeScript app with server actions over Postgres. Designed the AI layer as a single governed gateway supporting Gemini 2.5 Flash, Kimi, and Claude Sonnet, switchable from admin settings. Architected agents as recommend-only by construction: episode briefings, stalled-work detection, and recovery-plan drafts operate on permission-filtered views, cannot write data, and emit audit records on every call. Authored AWS target architecture (ECS Fargate, Bedrock, S3) with service-by-service cost model showing $300–450/month consolidated on AWS against $800–870/month retaining Supabase. Led database cutover and ported prototype into production application; normalized 65-table hx.* schema now carries row-level security on 34 tables.

experience.title: AI Engineer
experience.summary: Own the LLM integration layer of an adaptive learning platform that assesses a learner's existing knowledge of a certification and generates coursework covering only the gaps; 111 of 140 commits on the main line across a five-person team, backed by 72 tests. Built a structured completion client over LiteLLM with validation retry and JSON-mode fallback, enforcing two-layer Pydantic schemas across all four pipeline stages so provider-shaped responses never leak into domain types. Moved question-type allocation out of the prompt into deterministic Python with post-validation retry. Diagnosed persistent HTTP 402 'insufficient credits' error as burst-rate throttling, replacing LiteLLM's built-in retry with tenacity exponential backoff (10s floor). Traced a 500-ing course-list endpoint to select_related pulling 10–26MB JSON payload columns into a sorted query, overflowing MySQL sort buffer on 17 rows; rewrote to explicit .values() projection. Defined answer-key stripping contract after expanding assessments to four question types.

experience.title: Founding Engineer
experience.summary: Co-founded a HIPAA-compliant AI scheduling assistant for dental and physician offices; owned the AWS architecture and cost model while co-founder owned Terraform provisioning and DNS. Reached working pre-launch POC with architecture and compliance design settled. Argued for Bedrock over direct provider APIs on compliance grounds – already signing AWS BAA for RDS and S3, and any third-party LLM would need separate BAA negotiation. Caught that CloudTrail logs AWS API actions but not application-layer access to patient data, so specified conversation-level audit logging separately. Revised infrastructure cost model service by service, correcting Lambda cost as duration-bound rather than request-bound; POC estimate moved from blended $148 to roughly $115/month. Specified prompt caching on system prompt and per-practice config, projected to cut roughly 90% of dominant input cost. Built and shipped public marketing site in Next.js static export in a single day.

experience.title: Machine Learning Intern
experience.summary: Built a real-time computer-vision exercise-assessment system in Python and MediaPipe, holding form-detection latency under 100ms per frame through pose-landmark extraction and joint-angle calculation, delivering sub-second corrective feedback so users self-corrected during live sessions without instructor oversight. Cut counting errors from 20 to 14 over 200 ground-truth reps (over 92% count accuracy across kettlebell front raises, seated leg extensions, and jack knives) by adding calibration routines and motion-consistency checks rather than a heavier model, keeping latency budget intact; form-error events requiring coach intervention dropped from 50 to 30 on the same test set.

projects.name: RepoModernizer
projects.description: Built a 5-node LangGraph state machine (ingest, install deps, plan, migrate-file loop, finalize) that plans a file-by-file migration from a natural-language goal, rewrites each file with an LLM, and gates any diff above a risk threshold behind a human-in-the-loop interrupt() before it touches disk. Computed diffs from known-good before/after content rather than trusting LLM-authored diffs, with bounded retries and Bedrock primary/fallback failover on transient errors, plus guardrails (forbidden paths, max changed lines, no deletions) and a hard per-task cost cap evaluated against estimated spend before each call. Fixed a concurrency defect where repeated approve clicks produced 6–9 duplicate commits, using a pending-interrupt check plus an atomic DynamoDB claim so exactly one resume wins. Root-caused a git apply rejection affecting roughly a third of files (10 of 31) to diff generation force-padding a trailing newline onto both sides. Ran 16 real migrations at $0.0023 and 4.8 minutes average per run on a deliberately NAT-free stack (API Gateway, Lambda via Mangum, SQS, one-shot Fargate, EFS-mounted workspace, DynamoDB checkpointing); provisioned via Terraform and GitHub Actions OIDC, 96 passing tests, no long-lived AWS credentials.

projects.name: TerraformAgent
projects.description: Built a 6-node LangGraph pipeline (orchestrator, researcher, parallel domain subagents, aggregator, reviewer, evaluator) that turns a natural-language infrastructure request into validated Terraform, with a conditional edge that reruns only the domains a review flags, up to a capped number of targeted retries. Gated output on a real compiler: the evaluator writes generated code to disk and runs terraform fmt and terraform validate against a provider cache baked into the Docker image, reaching full offline validation by copying the read-only cache into a writable path once per execution environment. Instrumented the targeted-retry loop and measured it across 10 real prompts in both modes: zero pass-rate improvement (the same 4 of 10 passed) at 46s to 145s average wall time. Hardened review with a multi-LLM security fan-out (reusing the mcp-second-opinion pattern) querying OpenAI and Anthropic in parallel and blocking on any veto, degrading to single-LLM review on provider outage. Deployed the containerized service on Lambda and Step Functions with JWT authentication, DynamoDB state, SQS failure handling, and Secrets Manager; provisioned through Terraform and GitHub Actions OIDC, with 94 passing tests and no long-lived AWS credentials.

projects.name: EvalBench
projects.description: Architected a pluggable-suite eval harness where every benchmark emits one shared MetricRecord contract persisted to a single JSON-column table, so adding a suite is a three-file change that never touches the runner, store, or dashboard core. Shipped 3 benchmark suites on that harness: structured-output reliability (schema-valid rate, retries-to-valid, retry-only cost accounting), latency/cost with pairwise judge scoring, and RAG with recall@k, nDCG@k, and faithfulness across swappable chunking strategies. Ran 27 evaluation runs across 75 tasks and 7 model/config variants, surfacing an 8-point first-attempt schema-validity gap between providers on structured output and a p95 latency spread of 6.0s vs 9.4s; found that semantic chunking doubled RAG context precision (0.13 to 0.26) over fixed-window at comparable faithfulness. Hand-implemented statistically honest aggregation, attaching 95% Wilson intervals to proportions and binomial order-statistic intervals to p95 latency, with per-metric sample sizes on every leaderboard cell so no aggregate renders as a bare mean. Deployed serverless on AWS: dual Lambda (API plus async runner), API Gateway v2, CloudFront, DynamoDB run tracking, and SES magic-link auth; backed by 262 passing tests using injected LiteLLM callables and temporary SQLite databases, running the full suite with no provider calls or model cost.

projects.name: Wingman
projects.description: Designed a worker-evaluator state machine in LangGraph where a structured-output evaluator checks worker responses against user-defined criteria and reinjects feedback for up to 5 retry turns, raising answer-validity rates before surfacing a result. Made the agent serverless-safe by reconstructing LangGraph state from DynamoDB on every request instead of an in-memory checkpointer, eliminating cold-start state loss across Lambda invocations. Integrated 5 tool domains through LangChain ToolNode and bind tools: web search (Serper), Wikipedia, sandboxed Python REPL, sandboxed file I/O, and Pushover notifications, and shipped the full serverless stack (containerized FastAPI on ECR, Lambda, API Gateway v2, CloudFront) via the same OIDC pipeline.

projects.name: Twin
projects.description: Built a streaming personal-website agent using Titan-embedding retrieval over a persona corpus, grounded in a profile assembled at Lambda cold-start from a LinkedIn PDF, career summary, and style guide (parsed via pypdf) and injected into a Bedrock Claude Sonnet system prompt. Shipped a public evals dashboard scoring retrieval quality (recall@k, nDCG@k) on 35 labeled queries per push and LLM-judged faithfulness on live traffic via an S3-event-driven judge Lambda that adds zero latency to chat responses. Cut full-stack deployment to a single command across dev, test, and prod by chaining Docker build, Lambda upload, Terraform apply, Next.js export, S3 sync, and CloudFront invalidation through GitHub Actions and AWS OIDC.

projects.name: mcp-second-opinion
projects.description: Built and published an MIT-licensed MCP server that lets any MCP-aware agent consult rival LLMs (OpenAI, Gemini, Anthropic, Grok) mid-conversation, exposing two tools: one to query a single model and one to fan out to all enabled providers in parallel and compare answers. Unified four provider APIs behind a single LiteLLM interface, returning per-call latency, token counts, and cost; gracefully disables providers with no API key instead of failing, and ships as a pip-installable CLI (71 downloads in its first month) registered through standard MCP client config.
